newsitem.title: USA: Miss. court rules tobacco Medicaid suit can proceed.
newsitem.headline: Miss. court rules tobacco Medicaid suit can proceed.

text.p: The Mississippi state Supreme Court has ruled in favor of the state's attorney general and against Gov. Kirk Fordice's challenge to a $940 million tobacco lawsuit, a spokesman for Mississippi Attorney General Mike Moore said Thursday.
"It looks like they ruled for us," said Special Assistant Attorney General Trey Bobinger. He provided no further details, but said a news conference had been scheduled for 2:30 P.M. CST.

Fordice, a Republican, challenged the suit claiming that only he had the authority to bring lawsuits to recover Medicaid money since that state's division of Medicaid is under the control of his office.
If the court had ruled in Fordice's favour, Moore's lawsuit would have been limited to claims on behalf of charity hospital spending and the prohibition of cigarette advertising aimed at children.
Mississippi became the first state to file a Medicaid suit on May 23, 1994. Since that time, a total of 22 attorneys general and the lieutenant governor of Alabama have filed similar suits.
